messages.content:
For breakfast I had a 12 ounce iced coffee and a banana.

For lunch I had a quesadilla

Breakfast four ounces of asparagus, two eggs, one piece of gluten free bread.

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

Then breakfast again: four ounces of asparagus, two eggs, one piece of gluten free bread. That seems like they had breakfast twice? Maybe they had breakfast earlier and then had another breakfast? Or maybe they meant dinner? But we should interpret as they had breakfast items: iced coffee, banana, asparagus, eggs, bread. And lunch: quesadilla. We need to log each food item with portion size and meal. Use function calls. We have to call log_food for each item. The function signature: food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit (optional), meal_name. We need to decide portion units. For iced coffee: 12 ounces. Banana: maybe 1 banana? But portion unit could be pieces. For banana, portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: pieces. For quesadilla: portion_amount: 1, portion_unit: pieces. For asparagus: 4 ounces. Eggs: 2 pieces. Bread: 1 piece. Meal names: breakfast or lunch. For breakfast items: iced coffee, banana, asparagus, eggs, bread. For lunch: quesadilla. So we need to call log_food five times for breakfast items and once for lunch. Let's do that.
